circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, was designed by Hermann Tilke and has served as the venue for Formula One's season-closing Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. It represents the second of four Middle Eastern Formula One circuits, following Bahrain and preceding those in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year alongside various support categories including the Supercars Championship round. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 circuit licence.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit has a complex history as a venue for the Austrian Grand Prix. Originally established as the Österreichring, it hosted the race continuously throughout the 1970s and 1980s before undergoing reconstruction and renaming, eventually staging the grand prix again during the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital, situated along Baku Boulevard, spanning 6. 003 kilometers to rank as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit first hosted the 2016 European Grand Prix before being renamed to host the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km facility that has hosted various motorsport categories including the Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix, which marked the first F1 race held in the Middle East. The FIA Grade 1 licensed venue has accommodated numerous racing series such as GP2, Australian V8 Supercars (2006-2010), drag racing, and 24-hour endurance events, while offering multiple track configurations.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced design combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing multiple racing disciplines. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Situated in the Walloon region of Belgium near Spa, this 7. 004 km circuit has been a Formula One fixture since 1950, when it hosted a race during the championship's inaugural season. The venue has maintained annual Grand Prix status since 1985, missing only the 2003 and 2006 editions, establishing itself as a cornerstone of the modern F1 calendar.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, this 4. 361-kilometre circuit hosts the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix annually. Beyond F1, the venue has accommodated various international racing series including world sportscar championships, open-wheel competitions, and NASCAR events.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, the Shanghai International Circuit is renowned for hosting the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The venue has expanded its motorsport calendar to include electric racing championships alongside the traditional Formula One event.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone in Northamptonshire, England, this racing facility hosted the inaugural World Championship Grand Prix in 1950 and has served as the primary venue for Britain's Formula One race since 1987, following decades of sharing hosting duties with other circuits. The track also stages the British MotoGP round alongside its motorsport calendar.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Hungary, is a 4. 381 km permanent circuit that hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix held in Eastern Europe when it opened in 1986. Built in just eight months, the fastest construction timeline for any F1 venue, it was created outside the city near a highway after plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park were rejected.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Monza's 5. 793 km track near Milan has hosted the Italian Grand Prix almost continuously since 1949, making it one of the longest-running Formula One venues on the calendar. Constructed in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing circuit, it earned the nickname "Temple of Speed" for its characteristic long straights and fast-paced corners that promote high-speed racing.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807-kilometer Japanese racing facility situated in Mie Prefecture and operated by Honda Mobilityland. Renowned for hosting Formula One and Super Formula competitions, the track accommodates up to 155,000 spectators.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street track that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, running alongside the famous Las Vegas Strip section of Las Vegas Boulevard. The 3. 78-mile layout weaves past iconic resort properties and entertainment venues, creating a unique urban racing environment in one of the world's most recognizable entertainment destinations.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez honours brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both of whom died in racing accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue has periodically hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix, most recently from 2015 onwards on its current layout, with the event now officially designated as the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners and a qualifying average speed of approximately 139 mph. Designed by specialist track architects Apex Circuit Design, it was purpose-built to host the Miami Grand Prix when the event joined the Formula One calendar in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a compact 3. 337 km street course that winds through Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, incorporating the harbour area of the principality. Though technically spanning multiple Monaco neighborhoods, the circuit is universally known as Monte Carlo due to its predominant location within that district.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the Dutch Grand Prix after its Formula One return in 2021, though this arrangement concluded in 2026. The venue, situated just inland from the North Sea, had previously operated under different naming arrangements before its current sponsorship designation took effect in mid-2025.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a Qatari racing venue situated north of Doha near the city of Lusail, spanning 5. 419 kilometers with a lengthy main straight of 1. 068 kilometers.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian circuit in São Paulo, opened in 1940 and later renamed in 1985 to commemorate local Formula 1 driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years prior. The counterclockwise layout features modern racing facilities alongside a karting venue dedicated to fellow Brazilian motorsport legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along Jeddah's waterfront in Saudi Arabia, where it has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix annually since 2021. The track's scenic location borders the Red Sea and has recently expanded its motorsport calendar to include international electric racing events.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's downtown waterfront area, incorporating sections of the city's core planning districts along the bay. This urban circuit hosts the Singapore Grand Prix, one of Formula One's distinctive night races held on city streets.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, this 4. 657 km facility offers a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a comprehensive test for racing machinery. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and features grandstand seating for approximately 140,700 spectators.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: COTA is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 circuit in Austin, Texas that serves as the permanent home of Formula One's United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the facility hosts major international motorsport events including MotoGP's Americas round, the Lone Star Le Mans endurance race, and various other series, having previously accommodated IndyCar, rallycross, and sports car competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon represents Thailand in Formula One, competing for the Williams team. The driver holds both Thai and British nationality and continues his career in the sport.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has secured two world championships (2005 and 2006 with Renault) and 32 Grand Prix victories over 23 seasons. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved significant endurance racing success, including the 2018-19 FIA World Endurance Championship and two victories at Le Mans, making him the only driver to win both F1 and world-level sportscar championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli races for Mercedes in Formula One, having claimed seven race victories following his series entry in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One for Audi, bringing his racing talents to the German manufacturer's grid campaign.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Valtteri Bottas is a Finnish driver currently competing in Formula One for Cadillac. The 13-season veteran has secured two runner-up championship finishes during his Mercedes years (2019 and 2020) and has claimed 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Argentine driver Franco Alejandro Colapinto currently races in Formula One for the Alpine team. He represents one of the sport's emerging talents from South America in the global championship.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan combines reserve duties for Haas in Formula One with racing prototypes in the European Le Mans Series, having made seven Grand Prix appearances during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: French driver Pierre Gasly currently competes in Formula One for Alpine. He secured a race victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix during his time with AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a French-Algerian driver who currently races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, competing under the French nationality.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who has secured seven world championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. The veteran competitor holds multiple all-time records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently competes in Formula One for Audi, bringing significant experience from his extensive career in the sport. Beyond his Formula One commitments, he has achieved notable success in endurance racing, including a victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand racing driver currently competing in Formula One with Racing Bulls.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver competing for Ferrari, finished second in the 2022 World Drivers' Championship. Across his nine seasons in Formula One, he has secured nine Grand Prix victories.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish racing driver who competed in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and 2022-2024. Currently, he competes as a factory driver for BMW in the FIA World Endurance Championship with WRT, while also participating part-time in NASCAR's top series with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British competitor in Formula One, secured the drivers' championship in 2025 while racing for McLaren. The driver has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently competing for Haas. The driver achieved a Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian round while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from 15 seasons in the sport. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull and has secured six Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver, has secured nine Grand Prix victories during his Formula One career with McLaren, achieving these wins across four seasons of competition.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One between 2011 and 2024, earning the nickname "the Honey Badger" during his 14-season career. He secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his time in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell competes at the highest level of motorsport for Mercedes, having secured seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-year Formula One career.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during the 2023-2024 seasons. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category for Proton Competition, following previous experience in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll, a Canadian racing driver, currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One competition.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese racing driver currently holding a reserve position with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls. After competing as a full-time Formula One driver from 2021 through 2025, he transitioned to a backup role for the 2026 season.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, where he has claimed four consecutive world championship titles spanning 2021 to 2024. Throughout his 12-season career, he has secured 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is China's sole Formula One competitor, having raced in the sport from 2022 through 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac. As the only Chinese driver to have participated in F1, he represents a significant milestone for motorsport representation from his nation.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed under the Alpine banner since 2021, adopting the brand name to highlight Renault's sports car division while maintaining its status as Renault's factory operation. Previously known as Renault F1 Team and backed by Groupe Renault and the Renault-Nissan-Mitsubishi Alliance, the squad represented the manufacturer's works effort until Renault's withdrawal from the sport at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automobile manufacturer, has competed in Formula One through multiple organizational structures, with the current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, stands as Formula One's longest-tenured and most accomplished competitor, participating in every championship season since the sport's inception in 1950. Recognized by their iconic horse emblem, the team has maintained continuous involvement in the sport longer than any other rival outfit.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American-licensed Formula One team in 2014, with the squad entering the sport's world championship in 2016. Following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024, Ayao Komatsu assumed leadership as team principal.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: The Swiss engineering and racing operation founded by Peter Sauber in 1970 initially found success in sports car competition before joining Formula One in 1993. Over its three-decade F1 tenure, the independent constructor became the sport's fourth-longest-serving team by race entries before being acquired by Audi in 2024 to establish the foundation for Audi's return to the championship.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One team headquartered at its Technology Centre in Woking, operating as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group under ownership by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with its current iteration based in Brackley and operating under a German licence. The team, now known as Mercedes-AMG Petronas, became jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff from January 2022. Mercedes-entered teams are traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows" in motorsport circles.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as the second team owned by Red Bull GmbH alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with additional facilities near their sister team in Milton Keynes, the squad operates as part of Red Bull's expanded presence in the sport.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as the second team under Red Bull GmbH's ownership, alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with additional operations near Milton Keynes, the team operates as a sister squad within the Red Bull organization.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, based in England but licensed under Austria, is a dominant Formula One team established in 2005 as part of the Red Bull GmbH motorsport portfolio. Led by Christian Horner from its inception through 2024, the team transitioned to Laurent Mekies as team principal in 2025. Red Bull GmbH also operates a second F1 outfit through Racing Bulls.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, which competes as Atlassian Williams F1 Team from 2026, is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following the collapse of Williams's previous racing venture. Based at their Grove facility in Oxfordshire, the team has operated as a constructor and competitor since its formation.
